title: Who will win Eurovision Asia?
description:
Eurovision Song Contest Asia is happening for the first time in history! Expect a twerking Filipina, a KPop boyband star and a Mongolian dressed as a warrior…

Eleven countries will be competing to be the first ever winner of the singing competition. Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Mongolia, Bhutan, Philippines, Bangladesh, Thailand, South Korea, Nepal and Malaysia will all be involved in Saturday’s final. William Lee Adams, What in the World’s resident Eurovision expert, explains why the competition has been created, who the favourites are and some of the controversies that have surrounded the event.

Instagram: @bbcwhatintheworld Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Hannah Gelbart Producers: Mollie Perella, Adam Chowdhury and William Lee Adams Editor: Verity Wilde
summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討即將於曼谷登場的首屆亞洲歌唱大賽 Eurovision Song Contest Asia 的盛況。節目邀請 Eurovision 專家 William Lee Adams 剖析賽事背景、熱門奪冠人選與幕後風波。本屆共有 11 個國家參賽，市場預測大熱門包含馬來西亞歌手 Aina Abdul、越南歌手 Thảo Trang 及菲律賓歌手 Karmel，南韓則派出前 2PM 成員 Jun. K 參賽。節目亦分析了賽事預算遭刪減 100 萬美元與團隊人事變動等爭議，並指出該比賽為亞洲各國提供了凝聚人心與展現文化的舞台。
summaryEn: In this episode of What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart and Eurovision expert William Lee Adams discuss the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia taking place in Bangkok. Eleven countries are competing, with Malaysia's Aina Abdul, Vietnam's Thảo Trang, and the Philippines' Karmel highlighted as top favorites according to bookmakers, alongside South Korea's K-pop entry by Jun. K. The episode also touches on behind-the-scenes controversies—including a $1 million budget cut and changes to the international production crew—and explores how the contest provides Asian nations with a platform to celebrate their diverse cultures and unity.
